cohort: 221 women in singleton-gestational labor ≥ 37 weeks with cephalic fetuses
finding: While not predictive of delivery type, a narrower PAA was associated with the persistence of occipital varieties after birth.
mod_finding: While not a predictor of delivery type itself, a narrower pubic arch angle (PAA), as measured by transperineal ultrasonography during labor, was associated with the persistence of occipital varieties after birth.
